endorsements.quote: Similarly, we propose that ML algorithms should enter a period of phased introduction that will involve an initial trial period for the algorithm to observe , operate alongside clinicians, and adjust to local working practices and systems.
We propose analogous local and national regulations for ML algorithms to ensure that they are consistently pertinent and useful in the ever-changing landscape of clinical practice.
For instance, a threshold will need to be predetermined to trigger the re-evaluation of algorithm performance at a fixed interval or when a deterioration in performance is detected.
The proposed regulatory pathway aims to engineer a performance monitoring and adaptation system on a local and national level that aims to detect, monitor, and mitigate the effect of model drift.

Locally, we propose for institutions to curate their own test sets containing representative cases that better reflect the variability in equipment, protocol, epidemiology, and patient populations encountered at the deployment site.
The governing responsibility should be shared among clinicians, managers, software engineers, parent company representatives, and patients.

In addition, regulatory frameworks worldwide should emphasize the importance of equity and accessibility in the development of ML algorithms, taking into consideration resource-limited hospitals and countries, optimizing the use of available resources while optimizing the performance of the ML algorithms.

unlisted_practices: Establish an independent national regulatory body to set standards for algorithm development on data size and quality, technical assurance, and clinical safety.
Form national governance structures of appointed experts to curate a golden test set of cases defining minimum algorithm competence, and update it as clinical practice changes.
Retrain models on curated local training data when local testing shows deficiencies, while keeping the algorithm from deviating substantially from its initial objectives.
Have a sustainable substitute in place to maintain standard of care when an algorithm is suspended for retraining and evaluation.
Recruit a representative mix of internal and external clinicians for ground-truthing to minimize bias.
Provide resource-limited hospitals with a network of external ML experts and specialist hardware and software to support local implementation, monitoring, and evaluation.
Use federated learning to train models across multiple sites without physically exchanging patient data.
Incorporate ML into the medical curriculum and train clinicians to adapt continually to retrained algorithm behavior.
Assess proposed algorithms for clinical value, usability, cost-effectiveness, and sustainability before development to direct resources appropriately.

screen.reason: This is a viewpoint/framework paper proposing a novel regulatory pathway for AI/ML algorithms in health care analogous to the regulation of medical professionals.
